page: Amazon Web Services r8id.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs running at 3.9 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system integrates 480 MB of L3 cache alongside specialized instruction sets including AVX-512, Intel AMX (tile and int8), and cryptographic acceleration extensions. Dedicated compute capacity is paired with 768.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is addressed locally via 5,700 GB of high-throughput NVMe SSD instance storage, supplemented by a 40 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. No physical GPUs are present.

Benchmark data highlights the instance's high-throughput capability across both compute and memory subsystems. In multi-threaded computational workloads, the server records a Geekbench multi-core score of 22,271.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 107,072.92, both falling in the top tier (top 10%). Multi-core stress-ng tests reach 103,758.81, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 658.28 GB/sec. Memory subsystems demonstrate high bandwidth, achieving 384.81 GB/sec on uncached large-block read operations and 7,671.61 GB/sec on cached 16 KB read blocks. Single-threaded performance sits lower, with stress-ng single-core output in the average category at 2,121.4 and Geekbench single-core reaching 2,184.0.

From an operational perspective, the large DDR5 memory pool and high local NVMe storage volume offer strong resource density for data-intensive processing without requiring external network-attached block devices. High parallel execution efficiency is reflected in database and in-memory key-value tests, where PassMark database operations hit 33,271.24 and Redis SET throughput achieves 172.71 million operations per second. However, single-core execution speeds and generative LLM token generation rates (such as 4.58 tokens per second on a 70B model) remain moderate compared to the top-tier prompt processing throughput.

The hardware configuration suits large-scale memory-intensive workloads, including in-memory caches, distributed databases, large relational database engines requiring fast local scratch storage, real-time analytics, and heavy code compilation pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r8id.24xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server driven by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with 96 vCPUs (48 physical cores) at 3.9 GHz and 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory. Operating on the AWS Nitro system with an x86_64 architecture, it incorporates 480 MB of L3 cache and advanced instruction sets including Intel AMX and AVX-512. The instance bundles 5,700 GB of fast local NVMe SSD storage and a 40 Gbps baseline network interface, without discrete GPUs. Benchmarks demonstrate top-tier multi-core execution (Geekbench multi-core 22,271.0) and memory throughput (384.81 GB/sec large-block read), excelling in database operations and Redis workloads reaching 172.71 million operations per second. With an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio and high local disk capacity, it delivers high resource density for in-memory databases, real-time analytics, and large-scale data processing.
